newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crudes boosted by demand, strong arb.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crudes boosted by demand, strong arb.

text.p: U.S. demand for foreign crudes propped prices for North Sea and West African barrels in dealings Thursday, U.S. foreign crude traders said.
Wild trading ranges for the expiring NYMEX January crude contract kept the arb wide for WTI/Brent and West Africa.
IPE Feb Brent settled at $23.96, against the Feb WTI at $25.45 a barrel, a $1.49 spread.
The attractive North Sea arb and the good demand for early January has worked to depress Light Louisiana Sweet domestic grades against dated Brent, traders said.
Traders said the U.S. domestic grade market's volatility played with the true price of barrels, as moves ahed of the Thursday expiration for January NYMEX futures were seen.
"The U.S. refiners were short and waiting to cover themselves," said a trader.
Wet deals heard sold in the U.S. Thursday included a Jan 15-16 Nigerian Forcados cargo at dated Brent plus 77 cts, steady to slightly higher than recent trades confirmed at dated plus 75 cts.
A cargo of dated Brent loading on December 28-30 traded at January Brent minus 20 cts, 1.5 cts below the previous levels sold on Wednesday.
A pair of January 3-5 Brent cargoes were released from paper chains on Thursday, with J Aron clocked and Stasco keeping the other.
In the U.S. aftermarket, there were only two deals confirmed. A Jan/Feb Brent spread moved at 56 cts, with 200 lots of outright February Brent paper sold at $24.00.
Both parcels were sold to the same Wall Street trader.
